strings.name: Aitana Bonmatí
strings.summary: Aitana Bonmatí is a Spanish midfielder who developed in Barcelona’s academy into an important player for club and country. She helped Barça win the Women’s Champions League and Spain win the 2023 World Cup, receiving the tournament’s Golden Ball. She won three consecutive Women’s Ballons d’Or from 2023 to 2025, attracting international attention for her technique, playmaking and attacking contributions. After a serious leg injury in late 2025, she returned to club competition in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verified milestones through 2026-05-03; sources checked on 13 November 2026. This is not an event-by-event or live record.
strings.influence.rationale: A World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner, she has become an international representative of Spanish women’s football.

strings.highlights.worldcup.title: World Cup and tournament Golden Ball
strings.highlights.worldcup.text: She helped Spain win the 2023 Women’s World Cup and received its Golden Ball as best player; the championship was a team achievement.
strings.highlights.ballon.title: Three consecutive Women’s Ballons d’Or
strings.highlights.ballon.text: She won in 2023, 2024 and 2025, becoming the first player to win the women’s award three years running.
strings.timeline.return26.title: Returned after injury
strings.timeline.return26.text: After a serious left fibula injury in November 2025 and surgery, she returned as a substitute in the Champions League semi-final second leg against Bayern.
strings.timeline.ballon25.title: Third Women’s Ballon d’Or
strings.timeline.ballon25.text: She received her third consecutive Women’s Ballon d’Or in Paris, an individual award distinct from a team championship.
strings.timeline.cl24.title: Another Women’s Champions League title
strings.timeline.cl24.text: She helped Barcelona win the Women’s Champions League again in 2023/24 as part of the team’s sweep of that season’s trophies.
strings.timeline.nations24.title: Women’s Nations League title
strings.timeline.nations24.text: She helped Spain win the inaugural Women’s Nations League, extending the national team’s success to European competition.
strings.timeline.world23.title: World Cup and individual breakthrough
strings.timeline.world23.text: She helped Spain win the World Cup, received its Golden Ball and won her first Women’s Ballon d’Or that year.
strings.timeline.cl21.title: First Women’s Champions League title
strings.timeline.cl21.text: She helped Barça win its first Women’s Champions League and was named player of the final, a key turning point in her development.
strings.timeline.debut16.title: First-team debut
strings.timeline.debut16.text: She began playing for Barcelona’s first team and gradually became a regular, moving from academy football to the professional stage.
strings.timeline.academy12.title: Joined Barça’s academy
strings.timeline.academy12.text: At 14 she joined Barcelona’s academy, continuing her football development in the club system near her home.
